chapters.title: Chapter 5: Filing Your Return Step by Step

lessons.title: E-Verification: The Step That Makes Your Return Valid

body.text: Submitting your return is not filing it. Until you verify it, the department treats your return as unsigned paper. Miss the 30-day window and it is as if you never filed at all.

markDefs.definition: The electronic equivalent of signing your return, done through an Aadhaar OTP, net banking, an Electronic Verification Code, or a digital signature. Without it, a filed return is not treated as valid.

children.text: When you click Submit, the portal records your return data. But a return must be signed by you, and online that signature is

. Under CBDT Notification No. 5/2022, for returns filed on or after 1 August 2022 you must e-verify, or post a signed ITR-V, within 30 days of filing. The good news: for most people it takes under a minute.

stats.label: Time Limit
stats.context: From the date you file the return

stats.label: Aadhaar OTP Validity
stats.context: With 3 attempts to enter it correctly

stats.label: Ways to Verify
stats.context: Six electronic, plus ITR-V by post

body.caption: Verification Methods and What Each Needs

cells: Aadhaar OTP
PAN linked with Aadhaar, and access to the mobile number registered with Aadhaar
Most individual filers
Net banking
PAN linked to your bank account, with net banking enabled
Anyone whose Aadhaar-registered mobile is outdated
EVC through bank account
A pre-validated and EVC-enabled bank account on the portal
People who set this up while pre-validating their refund account
EVC through demat account
A pre-validated and EVC-enabled demat account
Investors with an active demat account
EVC through bank ATM
An ATM card linked to your PAN, from a participating bank: Axis, Canara, Central Bank of India, ICICI, IDBI, Kotak or SBI
Those without net banking
Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)
A valid Class 2 or Class 3 DSC on a USB token, with the emSigner utility running
Tax audit cases, where it is mandatory, and professionals
ITR-V by post
A printed, signed ITR-V acknowledgement posted to the Centralized Processing Centre in Bengaluru
A last resort when no electronic method works

events.title: Reach the Verification Page
events.description: Right after submitting, choose e-Verify Now. If you chose to verify later, log in and go to e-File, then Income Tax Returns, then e-Verify Return, or use the e-Verify Return link on the home page without logging in.

events.title: Pick Aadhaar OTP
events.description: Select the option to verify using an OTP on the mobile number registered with Aadhaar, and continue.

events.title: Give Consent
events.description: Tick the box agreeing to validate your Aadhaar details, and click Generate Aadhaar OTP.

events.title: Enter the OTP
events.description: Type the 6-digit OTP sent to your Aadhaar-linked mobile. It is valid for 15 minutes, and you get 3 attempts.

events.title: Confirmation
events.description: A success message with a transaction ID appears, and the acknowledgement is emailed to you. Your return status changes to verified.

body.title: The OTP Clock
body.textWithBlank: The Aadhaar OTP generated for e-verifying your return is valid for ___ minutes.
body.explanation: The OTP expires after 15 minutes and allows 3 attempts. If it expires, simply generate a new one. Keep your Aadhaar-linked phone with you before you click Generate.

body.title: When the OTP Never Arrives
body.question: Sunita, an accountant in Pune, files ITR-1 on 30 July 2026. Her Aadhaar is linked to an old mobile number she no longer uses. She has SBI net banking, and her PAN is linked to that account. What is her quickest way to verify today?
options: Aadhaar OTP, after waiting for the SMS to be forwarded
Log in to SBI net banking and use its e-filing option to e-verify
Print the ITR-V and post it to Bengaluru
Update her Aadhaar mobile number first, and verify after that
body.explanation: Net banking works as long as her PAN is linked to the bank account and net banking is enabled. It takes minutes. Posting ITR-V works but is slow and can get lost. Updating her Aadhaar mobile number is a good idea for the future, but it takes time she does not need to spend today.

body.title: What is an EVC, and how do I generate one in advance?

children.text: An Electronic Verification Code is a one-time code the portal sends to the mobile and email registered with your pre-validated, EVC-enabled bank or demat account, or that a participating bank's ATM generates when you use your PAN-linked card. You can generate it during the verification flow itself, or generate it in advance and then choose the option to verify with an EVC you already have. EVC can be enabled for only one bank account at a time, so enable it on the account whose mobile number you actually use.
The 30-Day Rule and What Late Costs

The 30 days run from the date you filed, not from the due date. If you verify after 30 days, the date of verification is treated as the date you filed the return, and every consequence of late filing follows. If you never verify, the return is treated as never filed. Filing on 31 July and verifying in September does not make you an on-time filer.

columns.label: Verified Within 30 Days
points: Your filing date is the date you submitted the return
If submitted by 31 July 2026, it is an on-time return

columns.label: Verified After 30 Days
points: Your filing date becomes the date of verification
If that falls after 31 July 2026, it is a late return
Late fee applies, and the old regime is no longer available
Most losses cannot be carried forward
Refund interest runs only from the date of verification

body.title: Find the Deadline
body.prompt: Farah files her ITR-1 on 28 July 2026 and picks e-Verify Later. Counting 30 days from the date of filing, what is the last date in August 2026 by which she must verify? Enter just the day of the month.
body.explanation: July 29, 30 and 31 are days 1 to 3. The remaining 27 days run to 27 August 2026. If she verifies by then, her return counts as filed on 28 July, before the due date. If she verifies on 28 August or later, the date of verification becomes her filing date, and her return becomes a late return.

body.title: Gaurav's Forgotten Click
body.scenario: Gaurav, a banker in Delhi with total income of ₹11 lakh in the old regime, files ITR-1 on 25 July 2026. His return shows a refund of ₹14,000, thanks to deductions for his parents' health insurance and a home loan. He clicks e-Verify Later, meaning to do it that evening, and forgets. He finally verifies on 5 September 2026.
body.prompt: What has Gaurav's delay cost him, and is there anything he can do?
body.modelAnswer: His 30-day window ended on 24 August 2026. Because he verified on 5 September, that date is treated as his filing date, which makes his return a late return filed after the 31 July due date. Three consequences follow. First, a late fee of ₹5,000, since his income is above ₹5 lakh. Second, a late return cannot use the old regime, so his tax will be recomputed under the new regime without the home loan interest and 80D deductions he planned his return around. Depending on his exact salary, his refund could change in either direction, but the choice is no longer his to make. Third, any refund interest runs only from the date of verification, not from 1 April. His remedy is a condonation of delay request on the portal, under e-File, explaining the reason for the late verification. Approval is discretionary, not automatic. The lesson for everyone else: verify immediately after submitting.

body.text: A condonation of delay request is a request, not a right. The department may accept a genuine reason, such as a hospitalisation, but it can also reject it. Treat e-verification as part of the filing, not a follow-up task.

children.text: If You Must Use ITR-V by Post

Download the ITR-V acknowledgement from the portal, print it, sign it, and send it by ordinary or speed post to: Centralized Processing Centre, Income Tax Department, Bengaluru 560500. It must reach CPC within 30 days of filing, so posting on day 29 does not work. Once received, the portal sends a confirmation, and the status of your return changes. Because it is slow and uncertain, use this only when every electronic method is unavailable.

body.label: Proof You Are Done
body.context: Check it under e-File, then Income Tax Returns, then View Filed Returns, and download the acknowledgement. Chapter 6 picks up from here: processing, refunds and intimations.

body.title: Verify Before You Close the Browser
steps: Before filing, confirm your PAN is linked with Aadhaar and your Aadhaar mobile number works
Keep a backup ready: net banking, or an EVC-enabled bank or demat account
Choose e-Verify Now right after submitting
Note the transaction ID and check the acknowledgement email
Confirm the status shows the return as verified under View Filed Returns
If you chose to verify later, set a reminder well within 30 days of the filing date

points: A submitted return is valid only once verified, electronically or by posting a signed ITR-V, within 30 days of filing under CBDT Notification No. 5/2022
Methods include Aadhaar OTP, net banking, EVC through a bank or demat account, EVC through a participating bank's ATM, a DSC, and ITR-V by post
The Aadhaar OTP needs PAN linked with Aadhaar, and is valid for 15 minutes with 3 attempts
Verifying after 30 days makes the verification date your filing date, bringing late fees, loss of the old regime option, lost loss carry-forward and later refund interest
An unverified return is treated as never filed, and a condonation of delay request is discretionary
ITR-V by post must reach CPC Bengaluru within 30 days, so e-verify immediately whenever possible

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax advice. Verification methods, participating banks, time limits and portal steps reflect the position at the time of writing and are set by CBDT notifications and portal updates that can change. Follow the current instructions on the Income Tax Department's e-filing portal or consult a qualified tax professional.
